note: Oak-hickory hills on Fiery Fork Creek and the Little Niangua River off Highway 7. The main primitive camp is a gravel loop with spurs and a privy at the end of a gravel road down to the Little Niangua; a second, smaller camp with a privy sits by a gravel turnaround off Granger Lane at the top of that road. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: area page 'Camping: Individual Campsites'; brochure 'Camping is allowed anytime in designated camping areas', 14 days in 30; map (11/14/2018) marks two Primitive Camping symbols, each with a privy: GIS 63 (pin, small turnaround off Granger Lane) and 62 (gravel loop by the Little Niangua, 1.24 km S, same entrance road). Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written manual. PIN: on the minor camp; the river loop is the clear main camp -> move to 38.07516,-92.95029. No split (shared entrance). Not waterfront kept. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Things to Do When You Visit': 'Camping: Individual Campsites'. Brochure: 'Camping is allowed anytime in designated camping areas. Stays are limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period. Groups of more than 10 campers require a special use permit.' The map (Last Updated 11/14/2018) legend has Primitive Camping; two symbols: (a) north, with Parking Lot, Privy and Disabled Accessible on Granger Lane; (b) south, with Parking Lot and Privy at the end of the road down to the Little Niangua River. GIS camping points 63 and 62 (Type 'Primitive Camping Area'). Imagery: 63 = a ~20 m gravel turnaround with a privy at the end of a ~100 m drive north of Granger Lane, the point 15 m N in the trees; 62 = a gravel camp loop ~110 x 50 m with several spurs, a central lot and a privy, ~55 m above the river. Designated camping at gravel lots, not boat-ramp lots; both stay. A 23-ft rig fits both. Access: ~1.2 km of gravel road down from Granger Lane to the river camp; no ford/4WD/rig wording.

PIN (main camp): stored 38.08565,-92.94538 = GIS 63, the minor north camp (point in trees 20 m N of its turnaround, lot 2488). The area's clear main camp is the river loop: move the pin to 38.07516,-92.95029 (GIS 62, in the middle of the loop). If AWH prefers to keep the north camp, move to its turnaround 38.08547,-92.94549 (lot 2488).

CLUSTERS / NO SPLIT: 62 is 1.24 km from 63, but its road branches off Granger Lane at the north camp, so the two share one entrance - no split. Nothing else in campgrounds.json lies within 3 km of 62.

WATERFRONT (not waterfront, kept, measured at the river loop): the loop's south spurs are ~55-65 m from the Little Niangua (~25-35 m wide) through woods on a bank (0.28 m/px leaf-off frame); no open apron, and no MDC photo shows a view. Not waterfront stands whichever camp the pin is on; the north camp is ~1 km from the river.
PHONE: area page and brochure '(573) 346-2210' (Camdenton) match.
